glosses: A needle without an eye (usually) made of drawn-out steel wire with one end sharpened and the other flattened or rounded into a head, used for fastening.

examples.text: With pins of adamant / And chains they made all fast.

glosses: A small nail with a head and a sharp point.
A cylinder often of wood or metal used to fasten or as a bearing between two parts.

examples.text: Pull the pin out of the grenade before throwing it at the enemy.

glosses: The victory condition of holding the opponent's shoulders on the wrestling mat for a prescribed period of time.
A slender object specially designed for use in a specific game or sport, such as skittles or bowling.
A leg.

examples.text: I'm not so good on my pins these days.

glosses: Any of the individual connecting elements of a multipole electrical connector.

examples.text: The UK standard connector for domestic mains electricity has three pins.

glosses: A piece of jewellery that is attached to clothing with a pin.

A simple accessory that can be attached to clothing with a pin or fastener, often round and bearing a design, logo or message, and used for decoration, identification or to show political affiliation, etc.

Either a scenario in which moving a lesser piece to escape from attack would expose a more valuable piece to being taken instead, or one where moving a piece is impossible as it would place the king in check.
The flagstick: the flag-bearing pole which marks the location of a hole
The spot at the exact centre of the house (the target area)

examples.text: The shot landed right on the pin.

glosses: The spot at the exact centre of the target, originally a literal pin that fastened the target in place.

examples.text:
For kings are clouts that euery man ſhoots at,
Our Crowne the pin that thouſands ſeeke to cleaue.
the very pin of his heart cleft

glosses: A mood, a state of being.

examples.text: Hee sett Promethius, on a merrye pynn, / Whoe dranke soe devillishly, that there he gott / A terrible heartburninge, […]
he had made the sign of the Cross on his head; for he was then on a merry pin and full of jearing

glosses: One of a row of pegs in the side of an ancient drinking cup to mark how much each person should drink.
Caligo.

examples.text: Blind with the pin and web

glosses: A thing of small value; a trifle.

examples.text: He […] did not care a pin for her.

glosses: A peg in musical instruments for increasing or relaxing the tension of the strings.
A short shaft, sometimes forming a bolt, a part of which serves as a journal.
The tenon of a dovetail joint.
A size of brewery cask, equal to half a firkin, or eighth of a barrel.

examples.text: Our ground crew were lodged in the main station, but they came to the cottage for a party when operations for the night had been cancelled and we had a new ‘gong’ (decoration) to celebrate. On these occasions we always installed a pin of bitter.

glosses: A pinball machine.

examples.text: I spent most of my time in the arcade playing pins.
Attracted by game operation, many invested heavily in pins and rolldowns prior to last spring.

glosses: A small cylindrical object which blocks the rotation of a pin-tumbler lock when the incorrect key is inserted.
An injection of PEDs.
To fasten or attach (something) with a pin.
To cause (a piece) to be in a pin.
To pin down (someone).

examples.text: He pinned his opponent on the mat.

glosses: To enclose; to confine; to pen; to pound.
To attach (an icon, application, message etc.) to another item so that it persists.

examples.text: to pin a folder to the taskbar

glosses: To fix (an array in memory, a security certificate, etc.) so that it cannot be modified.

examples.text: When marshaling data, the interop marshaler can copy or pin the data being marshaled.
[…] you can use the GCHandle class mentioned earlier to pin a heap block until you explicitly unpin it.

glosses: To cause an analog gauge to reach the stop pin at the high end of the range.

examples.text: Now I need to pin those needles.

glosses: To inject for performance enhancement.
To move a piece onto a blot, preventing the piece from further movement.
Alternative form of peen.
A cataract of the eye.

translations.source_sense_description: met een of meer spelden vastmaken

glosses: Attacher avec une épingle.

examples.text: Nous prenons deux otages, le vieux maire, […] et le jeune curé, […], bien que les soldats aient encore, épinglé à la capote, les Sacré-Cœur distribués à Paray-le-Monial.

Quelquefois, avant de me remettre un livre, maman en épinglait ensemble quelques feuillets ; dans La Guerre des Mondes de Wells, je trouvai ainsi un chapitre condamné. Je n’ôtais jamais les épingles, mais je me demandais souvent : de quoi est-il question ?

Elle avait attendu la visite de Poupette et de Lionel jusqu’à onze heures, dans l’angoisse, parce qu’on avait oublié d’épingler à son drap le cordon de la sonnette : le bouton était hors de sa portée, elle n’avait aucun moyen d’appeler.

glosses: Attraper.

examples.text: — Attention ! Voilà le commandant de La Mazardière… Ne me faites pas épingler, surtout !
Un silence nous épingle.

[…], pour éviter la tentation d'un ramponneau vengeur et ses emmouscaillements collatéraux, je me fais rare dans les parages.
D'autres, moins matois, se sont fait épingler.

glosses: Critiquer, pointer.

examples.text: D’une alternance à l’autre, les politiques se renvoient la balle, épinglant les programmes réécrits par leurs prédécesseurs ou la « baisse des horaires » (alors même que la France fait figure de championne en matière d’heures consacrées, à l’année, à l’enseignement des « fondamentaux »).
